before.guidance: Inspect the oral cavity and assess pain, ulceration, diet modification and interference with oral intake.

grades.label: Grade 0
grades.description: No oral mucositis.

grades.label: Grade 1
grades.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

grades.label: Grade 2
grades.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

grades.label: Grade 3
grades.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

grades.label: Grade 4
grades.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

after.guidance: Record the worst mucositis/stomatitis in the previous documented episode: oral pain, ulceration, dietary modification and ability to eat or drink. Do not substitute the current recovered grade for historical severity. NCCP 00596 v2 Table 3 uses grades 3 or 4 but does not name a grading edition. The CTCAE v5.0 oral-mucositis descriptions here are a user-interface grading aid, not an assertion of the edition used by NCCP; confirm the historical grade from the clinical record.
